Thought for 9s

You can now have multiple boards. Click the board name at the top (with the small arrow) to switch boards, or to create, rename or delete one. Your existing cards were moved into the first board, called "My board", and none were lost.

Separate boards: each board has its own three columns and cards.
Deleting: you're always asked to confirm first. When only one board is left, the delete option is greyed out and reads "Can't delete the only board".
Moving cards: a card's ⋯ menu now has "Move to board…". The card goes into the same column on the other board, at the bottom.
After a reload: your boards stay, and the board you were last on opens.

What I tested and how:

Automated logic tests: 35 pass, including 13 new ones.
Old saved data becomes the first board with every card kept.
With nothing saved, you start with one empty board.
Damaged new data falls back to the old data.
Creating, renaming and switching boards work, and a blank name is ignored.
Deleting a board makes a neighbouring board the open one, and the last board can never be deleted.
Each board keeps its own cards.
"Move to board" keeps the card's column.
New browser walkthrough at desktop (1280px) and mobile (375px): all 11 checks passed at both sizes. I started from data saved by the old single-board version and checked that:
all 4 old cards appeared in "My board", and its delete option was blocked;
renaming it, and creating "Work", worked; the new board started empty and opened straight away;
a card added to "Work" didn't appear on the other board;
"Move to board…" put a card from In progress into "Work"'s In progress column;
after a reload, "Work" was still the open board and its cards were all there;
deleting "Work" asked for confirmation (Cancel kept it, Delete removed it), after which the remaining board was protected again;
nothing scrolled sideways, and there were no page errors.
Earlier walkthrough re-run: all 21 original checks still pass at both sizes, including dragging by mouse and touch.
Visual check: the mobile screenshot shows the board name with its arrow, the moved card, and the "Moved…" notice.
